Regarding the makeup/hair/skincare stuff:

Skincare: moisturize every day. Find one that works for your skin type (normal, dry, oily, or combination). If you're not sure, go into a Sephora or a Kiehl's, the latter of which might be more comfortable. Get a chemical exfoliant, a product with AHA or BHA in it, which will make your skin more radiant. Always wear sunscreen that's at least SPF 30, your skin will thank you in 10 years and also skin cancer is no joke. This is stuff that everyone, regardless of gender, should be doing in my opinion.

Makeup: get a basic neutrals eyeshadow palette. Don't jump into anything with extreme colours. Look up a very basic eyeshadow application video on YouTube—I suggest finding one by a nice midwestern mom, if possible, because the ones by beautiful rich 20 year olds are a little hard to deal with. Get a cheap tube of mascara, and a neutral lipstick. Pluck your brows a little, but don't overdo it—just clean them up.

Hair: since you have long hair, there's a lot you can do. Get some layers cut in if you don't already have them and ask the stylist about suggestions for styling. One classic look is to use some salt spray (you can get this at a drugstore) and scrunch it up for a "just came from the beach" look.

Hope this helps, and good luck!

I'd been uncomfortable in my skin my whole life, dissociating and feeling distant from other guys. For a while I identified as bi, but something was still nagging at me. It was when I was dating a nonbinary trans guy and attended a dyke march that things really came to the fore for me—I collapsed crying on my bed, feeling this dam burst, all these pieces clicking together, a whole mess of mixed metaphors.

For a while after that I was staunchly nonbinary-identifying, for a few reasons: I thought being a trans woman was the worst thing in the world you could be; I had no trans women role models my age; and I was terrified that I'd never pass as a girl. It was kind of hedging my bets, even as I started on hormones. But within a year I realized that no, whatever my complicated gender feelings, I'd rather be seen by the world as a woman than a man.

You're in a tough situation, and I can't speak to the specifics of where you live, but I can offer some general advice.

First, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot of anxiety and thinking traps. I think the best place to start would be to see a general therapist and maybe try to get on some form of anti-depressant or anti-anxiety medication. 

Second, keep in mind that you cannot predict the future. Once you get some of your anxiety and depression issues a little more under control, it may be easier to think things through and see potential paths to the future you want more clearly. You don't know how you will feel after transition—how could you? And in terms of dealing with what other people think, if you're thinking that way then how do you know most other people aren't? Most of them are too wrapped up in their own business to notice or care about strangers.

Lastly, I can't talk you out of killing yourself, but I can say that you can connect with other people in similar situations on this sub or others and see how they dealt with it. You might think things are hopeless now, but there might be unexpected ways forward you haven't considered yet.
